key_insight: RoSHI fuses low-cost sparse IMUs with Project Aria egocentric cameras to recover full 3D human pose and body shape in a metric global frame, delivering portable, occlusion-robust, long-horizon human data capture in the wild.
problem_solved: Addresses the trade-off between portability, robustness to occlusion, and global spatial consistency when collecting rich, long-horizon human interaction data for scaling robot learning.
method: Hybrid wearable hardware: integrate sparse, low-cost IMUs on the body with Project Aria glasses for synchronized egocentric visual + inertial sensing.
Sensor-fusion pipeline that jointly estimates full 3D pose and parametric body shape in a metric global coordinate frame, mitigating occlusion and drift.
Lightweight, in-the-wild recording workflow designed for long-horizon interactions and downstream use in robot learning and imitation datasets.
impact: Makes scalable, real-world human demonstration data practical for robot learning, improving imitation, perception, planning, and sim‑to‑real transfer by providing globally consistent, occlusion-robust labels.
visual_elements: Schematic of the RoSHI wearable: Project Aria glasses + distributed sparse IMUs on a human silhouette
Pipeline flowchart: synchronized sensors → sensor fusion → metric 3D pose & body shape → global-frame alignment
Example scene overlays: real-world frames with estimated full-body pose under heavy occlusion
Comparison radar/bar chart showing trade-offs (portability, occlusion-robustness, global consistency) vs prior methods
paper_title: RoSHI: A Versatile Robot-oriented Suit for Human Data In-the-Wild
paper_authors: Wenjing Margaret Mao, Jefferson Ng, Luyang Hu, Daniel Gehrig, Antonio Loquercio
